title: the loop that runs
intent: The tick, the permission system, the tool registry and the session log exist as four modules that nobody calls. The claim the-agent-loop-is-wired is refuted, and it stays refuted until a dispatcher exists that takes one tick, asks the permission system whether the tool may run, runs it through the registry, and writes what happened into the append-only log. This wave is that dispatcher, and nothing else: the modules keep their APIs, and the order of the four calls is the order a reader would guess.
objection: A dispatcher that calls the four modules in the right order is still a dispatcher that knows nothing about what the model wants. The loop can be wired and still be a machine that walks a fixed path; the claim says the modules are reachable from one another, not that the loop is intelligent.
refuted_by: A check that walks a tick with a tool call that is denied by the permission system, and observes that no tool ran and that the denial is in the log. If the dispatcher can run a tool the rules forbid, the wiring is not the loop.
